US Investigates Strike in Iran, Trump Downplays Conflict

The United States is investigating a strike that hit a wedding party in Sirik, Iran. Senator JD Vance stated that the US military learns from its mistakes to improve, differentiating its approach from Iran's. Meanwhile, former President Donald Trump described the conflict with Iran as "small potatoes," noting that only 18 Americans had been killed and that the US was conducting "intermittent strikes" rather than actively fighting. Intelligence reports suggest Iran has gained a better understanding of its capabilities and the limits of US power after six months of conflict. The alliance between Jordan and the US makes the kingdom a target for Iranian strikes. In a separate case, the widow of a US airman was reportedly told the Iran conflict was "not technically a war" in a dispute over benefits following the crash of a KC-135 refueling aircraft supporting operations against Iran.
